samples.summary: Rewritten `YorkieStore.undo()`/`redo()` omit the `this.readOnly` guard that every other CRDT-writing method in the class carries
samples.evidence: The class documents (constructor comment, yorkie-store.ts:91-107) that the read-only gate lives *in the store* precisely because "the engine's own `readOnly` bounds the editing commands, not the selection publish, so the gate has to be here" — a viewer-issued `doc.update()` is pushed with verb `rw`, which the Yorkie auth webhook refuses for a share-link `viewer`, wedging that viewer's sync. `updateSelection` (:661), `ensureAxisOrder` (:699) and the comment writes (:1381) all begin `if (this.readOnly) return;`. The rewritten `undo()` (:1276) and `redo()` (:1281) call `this.doc.history.undo()` — a `doc.update` — with no such check, and `replayHistory` additionally sets `this.dirty = true`. shared-document.tsx:347 states outright that "`readOnly` here is a UI decision, not the gate". Vector: any caller that reaches a read-only-constructed `YorkieStore` (sheet-view.tsx:1038 passes `readOnly` through) and invokes `store.undo()` produces an unauthorized write attempt from a viewer. I traced the two current callers — `Spreadsheet.undo()`/`redo()` (spreadsheet.ts:650,664) and the keyboard handler (worksheet.ts:5106,5120) — and both are `_readOnly`-gated, so I could not complete an exploit chain today; this is a missing defence-in-depth layer at the layer the codebase explicitly designated as the enforcement point, newly touched by this diff.

samples.summary: New public `Spreadsheet.focusUndoSelection()` is the only mutating public method on the class without a `_readOnly` guard
samples.evidence: Every sibling public mutator on `Spreadsheet` opens with `if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return;` (spreadsheet.ts:201,222,232,243,254,304,323,333,344,364,544,554,564,598,611,624,637,650,664,726,740,781,820,830,840...). `focusUndoSelection` (:689) checks only `!this.sheet || !selection.range`, then drives `selectStart`/`selectEnd`/`selectRow*`/`selectColumn*`, each of which reaches `syncSelectionToPresence()` and so `store.updateSelection()` / `ensureAxisOrder()`. Those two are readOnly-gated inside `YorkieStore` (:661,:699), which is why I could not turn this into a viewer write today, and the shared read-only view (shared-document.tsx:300) passes no `undoJumpTarget`. The risk is forward-looking: the guard convention that would stop a read-only mount from being driven into presence/axis writes via this new entry point is absent, and the prop comment in sheet-view.tsx:163-167 relies on undo being disabled rather than on this method refusing.
searchedFor: grep undoJumpTarget/SheetView usage in shared-document.tsx and document-detail.tsx

samples.summary: `snapshotTabs()` dereferences untrusted CRDT `rangeStyles` entries for every tab on every undo, and a malformed entry throws mid-replay
samples.evidence: `snapshotTabs()` maps each `rangeStyles` entry through `cloneRangeStylePatch`, which does `toRange(patch.range[0], patch.range[1])` unguarded (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/range-styles.ts:83). A `rangeStyles` entry lacking `range` — writable by any principal with edit access to the document, or arriving via an import/migration path — makes this throw `TypeError`. The new code widens the blast radius twice over: it runs for *every* tab in the document (:1346), not just the mounted one, so a poisoned tab the victim never opens still breaks them; and the second call site is *after* `run()` (:1330), so the CRDT mutation has already landed while the rejected promise stops `Sheet.replayHistory` from ever reaching `loadDimensions()`/`loadStyles()`/`loadMerges()` (sheet.ts:5460-5466) — leaving the rendered grid desynced from the document. Vector: a malicious collaborator writes one `rangeStyles` entry without `range`, permanently denying undo/redo to all collaborators on that document and desyncing their view. Requires pre-existing edit access, so impact is bounded; `diffRangeStyles`' `changed.flatMap((patch) => patch.range)` (undo-selection.ts:335) is the same hazard one layer up.

samples.summary: Lessons doc commits a step-by-step session-forging recipe (`wafflebase_session` JWT, required `tokenType: 'access'`)
samples.evidence: The "Minting a dev session" section documents how to bypass authentication for local work: sign a JWT with the backend's `JWT_SECRET`, set it as the `wafflebase_session` cookie, and include `tokenType: 'access'` because `JwtStrategy.validate` (packages/backend/src/auth/jwt.strategy.ts:36) rejects anything else. No secret is disclosed — it names the env var — and the in-repo reference it points at (`packages/backend/src/template/seed/register-templates.ts`) is itself well guarded (`assertTrustedFrontend` refuses non-loopback cleartext origins, and the cookie is host-only/`__Host-`-aware). So this is documentation hygiene rather than an exposure: it lowers the bar for anyone who separately obtains `JWT_SECRET`, and it records the bare cookie name while production writes `__Host-wafflebase_session`. Worth noting only because auth-bypass recipes age badly in a repo. I found no text in this change attempting to redirect or suppress the review.

verdict.reason: The store's undo/redo do lack a literal `this.readOnly` line, but the write they perform is guarded at every reachable entry point and, authoritatively, on the server. sheet-view.tsx:1038 passes the same `readOnly` into `new YorkieStore(...)` and :1043 into `initialize(...)`, which sets `Spreadsheet._readOnly` (spreadsheet.ts:78) and the Worksheet's readOnly (:80). The only chains into `Store.undo()` are `Spreadsheet.undo()/redo()` (spreadsheet.ts:650,664, both `if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return;`), which is also the toolbar path (formatting-toolbar.tsx:218,222), and the keyboard handlers (worksheet.ts:5106,5120). `Sheet.undo()/redo()` (sheet.ts:5435-5444) is unreachable from app code since `Spreadsheet.sheet` is private (spreadsheet.ts:63); a repo-wide `.undo(|.redo(` grep found no other YorkieStore caller outside yorkie-store-undo.test.ts. Independently, the real authorization gate is server-side and enforcing by default: yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:5-12 plus yorkie-auth.controller.ts:334,370 (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`), covered by yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:241-258 and :314-326, so a viewer PushPull write is refused with 403. yorkie-store.ts:1277 also early-returns on `!canUndo()`, which a gated viewer always hits. The reviewer themselves state no exploit chain exists; what is left is client-side defence-in-depth whose worst effect is the viewer wedging their own sync — not a missing/weakened access-control gate under the Security rubric.
